wu: Students play 'Two Truths and a Lie' about their recent experiences using present perfect (e.g., 'I've visited Chefchaouen,' 'I've learned to make tagine,' 'I've met a tourist from America'). They guess which statement is false.
wuAlt: Students share one 'first time' using past simple (e.g., 'The first time I tried American food was...')
Students play 'Find Someone Who' using present perfect (e.g., 'Find someone who has visited the American Space')
pres: Display a PET reading part 1 text on the board. Model skimming for gist and scanning for specific information. Elicit strategies like 'read questions first' and 'underline keywords'. Check understanding with quick thumbs up/down for 'Do we read every word?'
presAlt: Show a sample PET writing task (email) and highlight structure: opening, purpose, details, closing
Play a short PET listening part 1 audio and model predicting answers before listening
prac: Students complete a timed PET reading part 2 (multiple-choice cloze) in pairs, discussing answers. Monitor and provide support with vocabulary hints. Then, they swap papers and mark using the answer key.
pracAlt: Students practice PET speaking part 1 (interview) with a partner, using prompt cards about travel and hobbies
Complete a guided PET listening part 2 gap-fill with word bank support
ls: Students listen to a PET listening part 3 (multiple matching) audio about a local festival (e.g., Green March). They match speakers to statements and then compare answers in pairs. Play audio twice.
re: Students stand in a circle. Teacher says a PET task type (e.g., 'Reading Part 1!'), and students quickly mime the action (e.g., 'skimming' with hands). Fast-paced to re-energize.
prod: Students work in groups to create a 3-minute PET speaking part 2 (long turn) prompt about 'a place you recommend in Morocco'. They take turns describing the photo and answering partner questions.
rw: Students write a timed PET writing part 1 (email) to a friend about a recent trip to Casablanca (80-100 words). Include past simple and descriptive adjectives. Peer-check for structure and word count.
st: Teacher shares a short video clip of an American tourist in Morocco, then closes with: 'Today we practiced PET test strategies. Thank you for your hard work. See you next week!'
g: Teams race to answer PET-style questions (reading, grammar, vocab) on the board
Students draw PET-related words (e.g., 'examination', 'certificate') for teammates to guess
Teams correct mistakes in PET sample sentences, then run to write the correct version
Students draw cards with PET speaking topics and respond for 1 minute
Groups read different PET reading texts and summarize key points for the class
diff: Fast finishers: Write a second PET email draft with more complex adjectives
Support learners: Use a sentence frame for the writing task (e.g., 'I went to... It was... because...')
hw: Complete a full PET reading part 4 at home and score yourself
Record yourself answering a PET speaking part 2 prompt and self-reflect
Review PET writing samples and write down 3 tips for improvement
tip: For Moroccan learners, connect PET tasks to local contexts (e.g., describing a souk, writing about Islamic holidays) to boost engagement and confidence.
